# Apple Makes Rare Admission of Regulatory Hit as App Store Commission Model Erodes, Weighing on $100 Billion Services Business
Apple has for the first time acknowledged in a regulatory filing that global antitrust actions are eroding its services business, which generates more than $100 billion in annual revenue. The company warned that transactions completed through alternative payment systems "may be entirely ineligible for commission." Sensor Tower data shows US App Store consumer spending fell 6% year-over-year in the second quarter, versus 9% growth a year earlier; Appfigures estimates Apple's US commission revenue has shrunk 18% so far this year. Apple's services revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 hit a record $30.7 billion but missed Wall Street expectations. CFO Kevan Parekh acknowledged that rule changes have already impacted the segment. Analysts note that Apple's premium valuation rests on its services business, and the market will be forced to reassess that segment's profitability.
##### Key Elements
[Apple](https://finance.biggo.com/s/Apple?hot_keyword=1)[App Store](https://finance.biggo.com/s/App%20Store?hot_keyword=1)[Epic Games](https://finance.biggo.com/s/Epic%20Games?hot_keyword=1)[Sensor Tower](https://finance.biggo.com/s/Sensor%20Tower?hot_keyword=1)[Appfigures](https://finance.biggo.com/s/Appfigures?hot_keyword=1)[Kevan Parekh](https://finance.biggo.com/s/Kevan%20Parekh?hot_keyword=1)[David Vogt](https://finance.biggo.com/s/David%20Vogt?hot_keyword=1)[Wamsi Mohan](https://finance.biggo.com/s/Wamsi%20Mohan?hot_keyword=1)[Nicholas Rodelli](https://finance.biggo.com/s/Nicholas%20Rodelli?hot_keyword=1)
Apple has for the first time explicitly acknowledged in its latest regulatory filing that intensifying antitrust regulatory pressure worldwide is materially eroding the core profit foundation of its services business. The company warned that purchases completed through alternative payment systems "may be entirely ineligible for commission" — a statement widely viewed as the clearest signal yet that the App Store commission model underpinning its high-margin services business is facing systemic loosening.
Earlier this month, Apple reported services revenue and margins that both fell short of Wall Street expectations. While services revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 reached a record $30.7 billion, growth momentum has visibly weakened. Apple CFO Kevan Parekh acknowledged during the earnings discussion that recent App Store rule changes have already had a tangible impact on the segment.
### Cracks in the Commission Model Under Regulatory Siege
Apple's grip on the App Store is being challenged simultaneously across multiple jurisdictions. Last year, game developer Epic Games accused Apple of monopolistic practices in violation of federal antitrust law, ultimately forcing Apple to allow app developers to direct users to alternative payment methods outside the App Store free of charge — bypassing its traditional commission mechanism.
The shockwaves from that ruling quickly reached consumers. According to mobile app analytics firm Sensor Tower, US consumer spending through the App Store fell 6% year-over-year in the second quarter, compared with 9% growth in the same period last year. Sensor Tower explicitly noted that the US slowdown reflects a "significant impact" on App Store consumer spending from the ruling.
Globally, consumer spending through the App Store grew just 3% year-over-year in the first half of this year, a sharp deceleration from 13% growth a year earlier. Sensor Tower also noted that weak consumer spending and macroeconomic uncertainty may have dampened demand to some degree.
Estimates from Appfigures, another app data research firm, are even more sobering: Apple's US commission revenue has contracted 18% so far this year. Appfigures research also found that App Store revenue in Brazil and Japan is contracting as well, following new regulatory measures introduced in those countries in recent months.
### Key Data at a Glance  
| Metric  | Value  | Comparison  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| US App Store consumer spending (Q2)  | Down 6%  | Up 9% a year earlier  |  
| Global App Store consumer spending (H1)  | Up 3%  | Up 13% a year earlier  |  
| US commission revenue (year-to-date)  | Down 18%  | —  |  
| FY2026 Q3 services revenue  | $30.7 billion  | Record but below expectations  |  
Note: Data sourced from independent research estimates by Sensor Tower and Appfigures.
### Analyst Divide: Currency Effects or Structural Shift?
Wall Street analysts are split on how to interpret the services slowdown. UBS analyst David Vogt bluntly characterized the App Store growth deceleration as a "concern," suggesting it may not be a short-term fluctuation. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan acknowledged that the $30.7 billion services figure set a record, but conceded it was "slightly below our expectations."
Apple management has attempted to attribute some of the earnings pressure to external factors such as currency fluctuations, but Parekh's candid admission of regulatory impact makes that explanation appear insufficient. Nicholas Rodelli, director of legal research at Washington Analysis, offered a sharper assessment: "Apple's premium valuation rests on its services business, and the App Store is at the heart of that business. We believe the market will reassess the profitability of the services segment."
Rodelli's judgment touches on a deeper issue: Apple's valuation logic has long relied on the high margins of its services business to offset cyclicality in its hardware segment. If App Store commission revenue remains under sustained pressure, investors may need to recalibrate fundamental assumptions about Apple's long-term profitability.
### Multi-Front Global Regulatory Assault
The regulatory pressure Apple faces is not an isolated event but part of a broader global antitrust wave. In the United States, the precedent set by the Epic Games case is being invoked by a growing number of developers; in Europe, the Digital Markets Act imposes strict obligations on large tech platforms, forcing Apple to open up sideloading and third-party payments; in Asia, regulators in Japan and Brazil have followed suit with new rules that further compress Apple's commission revenue.
Notably, Apple's language in the regulatory filing — "may be entirely ineligible for commission" — hints at a worst-case scenario of revenue falling to zero. While the phrasing carries the legal caution typical of risk disclosures, its appearance in Apple's official filing is itself a landmark event. Previously, Apple had consistently maintained that its commission model was a fair and reasonable industry standard, and had kept an optimistic tone about the potential impact of regulatory challenges.
The services business has long been the pillar of Apple's growth strategy. With hardware products like the iPhone facing slowing growth, Apple CEO Tim Cook has repeatedly emphasized services as the core engine of the company's transformation. Now, the fuel powering that engine is being progressively diminished by regulatory forces. Whether Apple can find alternative growth pathways will be a key focus for the market in the coming quarters.

# Apple’s Siri revamp reportedly delayed… again
Apple has been promising a new-and-improved, cutting-edge, AI-powered Siri since it first [unveiled](https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/10/apple-intelligence-is-the-companys-new-generative-ai-offering/) Apple Intelligence in 2024. Over about a year and a half since then, the release date for this new era of Siri has been continuously pushed back. According to a new [report](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-11/apple-s-ios-26-4-siri-update-runs-into-snags-in-internal-testing-ios-26-5-27) from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, we’ll likely have to wait even longer.
While the new Siri was expected to launch with the upcoming iOS 26.4 update in March, now, the changes are expected to roll out more slowly over time, reportedly postponing some features until the May iOS update, or even until the release of iOS 27 in September. Apparently, Apple ran into trouble when testing the software, requiring the launch date to be pushed back further.
The changes are rumored to make the longtime digital assistant more like the LLM chatbots that have swept the tech world — but instead of opening up a ChatGPT or Claude app on your iPhone or MacBook, you would be able to just talk to Siri, which will be powered by [Google Gemini](https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/12/googles-gemini-to-power-apples-ai-features-like-siri/).
We’re starting to feel bad for the Siri product managers. Hang in there, folks.

# Apple's US App Store Commission Revenue Down 18% This Year
Tuesday August 18, 2026 4:41 am PDT by [Tim Hardwick](https://www.macrumors.com/author/tim-hardwick/)
The commission Apple earns from the App Store is shrinking in markets where it has been forced to relax its grip on in-app purchases, based on new analytics data. 
According to Appfigures, cited by the ($), Apple's U.S. commission revenue has fallen 18 percent since the start of 2026. It also found App Store revenue declining in Brazil and Japan since both countries introduced new regulations.
Separately, Sensor Tower said U.S. consumer spending through the App Store was down 6 percent in the second quarter, compared to 9 percent growth a year earlier. 
The figures follow Apple's admission during last month's [earnings call](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/30/apple-3q-2026-earnings/) that regulatory changes have started to weigh on its Services growth. Apple reported services revenue of $30.7 billion for the June quarter, a record for the period but short of the $31.4 billion that analysts expected.
Apple traditionally has taken 15 to 30 percent of digital purchases made inside apps on the App Store. However, a U.S. [injunction](https://www.macrumors.com/2025/04/30/apple-app-store-anti-steering-injunction-violation/) won by Epic Games now forces the company to let developers steer users to outside payment options without taking a cut. Sensor Tower said the U.S. slowdown had been heavily affected by the ruling. Apple has not collected fees from link-outs in the U.S. since April 2025.

results.title: Apple's C2 Modem Arrives Faster Than Qualcomm Expected, Slashing Revenue by Half
results.summary: Tech Times (Jul 30, 2026), sourced from a Qualcomm Q3 FY2026 post-earnings Reuters interview (CEO Cristiano Amon) and earnings call (CFO Akash Palkhiwala). Reports Apple-related Qualcomm chip revenue will fall ~50% sequentially Sep-Dec 2026, faster than Qualcomm's own model anticipated, because component-supply constraints accelerated Apple's C2 modem rollout. Qualcomm's prior estimate of ~20% iPhone-18-lineup modem share is 'off the table' — actual share will be 'materially lower.' Amon: 'We kind of replaced Apple with the data center.' # Apple’s C2 Modem Arrives Faster Than Qualcomm Expected, Slashing Revenue by Half
#### Supply crunch cuts Qualcomm’s iPhone 18 slice well below 20%; automotive and data center bets accelerate.
By Published: Jul 30 2026, 2:12 PM EDT
[Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322279/20260730/apples-c2-modem-arrives-faster-qualcomm-expected-slashing-revenue-half.htm) [Share on Twitter](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=Apple%27s+C2+Modem+Arrives+Faster+Than+Qualcomm+Expected%2C+Slashing+Revenue+by+Half+https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322279/20260730/apples-c2-modem-arrives-faster-qualcomm-expected-slashing-revenue-half.htm) [Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.techtimes.com%2Farticles%2F322279%2F20260730%2Fapples-c2-modem-arrives-faster-qualcomm-expected-slashing-revenue-half.htm&title=Apple%27s+C2+Modem+Arrives+Faster+Than+Qualcomm+Expected%2C+Slashing+Revenue+by+Half) [Share on Reddit](http://reddit.com/submit?url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322279/20260730/apples-c2-modem-arrives-faster-qualcomm-expected-slashing-revenue-half.htm&title=Apple%27s+C2+Modem+Arrives+Faster+Than+Qualcomm+Expected%2C+Slashing+Revenue+by+Half) [Share on Flipboard](https://flipboard.com) [Share on Pocket](https://getpocket.com/edit?url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322279/20260730/apples-c2-modem-arrives-faster-qualcomm-expected-slashing-revenue-half.htm)
Apple.com
Qualcomm now knows exactly how fast it is losing Apple. On July 29, CEO Cristiano Amon disclosed in a [post-earnings Reuters interview](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/29/qualcomm-apple-modem-revenue-dropping/) that Apple-related chip revenue will fall roughly 50 percent sequentially between the September and December 2026 quarters — a sharper drop than the company had modeled, arriving sooner than its own guidance suggested. The catalyst is not a change of strategy but a change of pace: [supply constraints across the semiconductor industry](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29) have accelerated Apple's rollout of its in-house C2 modem, compressing the timeline in ways that Qualcomm's models did not anticipate.
That acceleration has a concrete financial signature. Qualcomm had previously estimated it would supply modems for roughly 20 percent of the iPhone 18 lineup — itself already a dramatic reduction from its historical near-total dominance of Apple handsets. That figure is now off the table. CFO Akash Palkhiwala told analysts on the earnings call that the company's actual share in the upcoming iPhone launch will be ["materially lower"](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29) than the 20 percent estimate. In plain terms, Qualcomm's last foothold in Apple's flagship line is shrinking faster than even the chipmaker expected.
"We kind of replaced Apple with the data center," Amon said in [a Reuters interview](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/29/qualcomm-apple-modem-revenue-dropping/) — a line that captures both the scale of what is being lost and the confidence with which Qualcomm believes it can absorb it.
### Qualcomm's Q3 Numbers: Strong Quarter, Steeper Cliff Ahead
The quarterly results themselves were solid. Qualcomm reported [fiscal third-quarter revenue of $9.9 billion](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29), landing at the high end of its own guidance and beating Wall Street's consensus estimate of $9.67 billion. Non-GAAP earnings per share came in at $2.21, broadly in line with analyst expectations. QCT — the chipmaking segment — contributed $8.5 billion, while the licensing arm QTL delivered $1.3 billion at a 69 percent earnings-before-tax margin.
But within those numbers, the handset division told a harder story. QCT handset revenue fell to $5.09 billion in the quarter, [down 20 percent year over year](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29), weighed down by unprecedented memory price inflation that pushed original equipment manufacturers toward lower-tier chips and older inventory. QCT gross margins fell below Qualcomm's historical 48-to-50-percent baseline range as a result.
For the fiscal fourth quarter — the period covering the iPhone 18 launch window — Qualcomm [guided to total revenue of $9.7 billion to $10.5 billion](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29), with QCT handset revenue of approximately $5.2 billion. Android growth is expected to partially offset the Apple shortfall. But the more consequential guidance was structural: [CFO Palkhiwala confirmed](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29) that the December quarter will no longer be Qualcomm's annual revenue peak. Revenue is now expected to grow from December into the March quarter — a direct inversion of the seasonal pattern that had governed Qualcomm's financial calendar for years, driven entirely by the Apple iPhone launch cadence that is now exiting the model.
### A Four-Year March Toward Modem Independence
The roots of this moment stretch back to 2019, when Apple [acquired Intel's smartphone modem division](https://www.macrumors.com/2024/01/31/apple-extends-qualcomm-modem-licensing-deal/) and began building its own baseband engineering teams and intellectual property portfolio. The first tangible result arrived in early 2025 with the iPhone 16e, which debuted the C1 — Apple's inaugural in-house 5G modem. Within six months, the upgraded C1X appeared in the iPhone Air, and by March 2026 the C1X had also landed in the iPhone 17e, cementing Apple's value-tier lineup on its own silicon.
Throughout the iPhone 17 generation, however, the flagship Pro models retained Qualcomm's Snapdragon modems — and for a technically specific reason. Apple's C-series chips have not yet achieved competitive mmWave 5G performance, the ultra-high-frequency band (24-to-100 GHz spectrum) that US carriers including Verizon and AT&T have invested billions to deploy in dense urban environments. mmWave delivers multi-gigabit throughput but has limited range and cannot penetrate buildings — it works in stadiums, transit hubs, and dense downtown corridors, and US buyers of premium iPhones use it there. Without matching Qualcomm's mmWave capability, Apple cannot universally deploy its own modem in the US Pro line without delivering a functionally inferior network experience to the buyers paying the highest price.
The next-generation C2 modem — internally codenamed Ganymede, manufactured on TSMC's 4-nanometer N4 process — is designed to change that calculus, but not yet for US buyers. Leaked supply chain intelligence, corroborated by multiple analysts, suggests that [international iPhone 18 Pro models will deploy the C2 while US models will retain a Qualcomm modem](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/319748/20260705/iphone-18-pro-leak-india-opens-criminal-probe-stolen-files-reveal-c2-modem-plans.htm) to preserve mmWave performance. The dual-modem approach — Apple silicon for the world, Qualcomm for the American market — means Qualcomm retains some presence in the flagship line. The question the Q3 earnings call answered is how small that presence will be: materially below 20 percent, and falling.
What the C2 brings that Qualcomm's Snapdragon does not offer is NR-NTN support — New Radio Non-Terrestrial Networks, a 3GPP Release 17 standard that enables a smartphone to connect directly to low-earth orbit satellites for broadband internet access, treating them like a very distant cell tower. This goes well beyond the emergency satellite SOS functions on current iPhones. International buyers of the iPhone 18 Pro will receive a modem that can access satellite broadband from LEO constellations — a capability no Qualcomm modem in current production matches.
**Read more:** [**iPhone 18 Pro Leak: India Opens Criminal Probe as Stolen Files Reveal C2 Modem Plans**](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/319748/20260705/iphone-18-pro-leak-india-opens-criminal-probe-stolen-files-reveal-c2-modem-plans.htm)
### The Long Game: Why This Transition Is Irreversible
The standard frame for the Apple-Qualcomm story is financial: Apple saves the Qualcomm royalty per unit and improves its margins; Qualcomm loses a key customer. That frame is accurate but incomplete. The deeper implication of Apple's modem vertical integration is architectural.
Qualcomm's Snapdragon modems are discrete chips that communicate with Apple's A-series application processor over a bus interface — a design that imposes a hard ceiling on how efficiently power can be managed across the system, because two separately designed chips must negotiate how they share thermal headroom and battery draw. Once Apple integrates the C-series baseband with the A-series SoC on a unified die or package — as it has already done with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and the Ultra Wideband chip — it will be able to optimize power draw and thermal output across the full compute stack in ways that a third-party modem supplier relationship structurally cannot replicate. The C1 and C2 are not yet integrated with the A-series SoC. They are the first steps toward that integration. When it arrives, no price concession or technical specification will make a return to an external modem commercially rational for Apple.
The royalty licensing relationship provides a financial bridge in the near term. Qualcomm's [patent licensing agreement with Apple](https://www.macrumors.com/2024/01/31/apple-extends-qualcomm-modem-licensing-deal/) — the successor to the 2019 settlement that ended a years-long legal dispute — runs through at least March 2027, continuing to generate licensing revenue from Apple even as chip revenue declines. That bridge softens the cliff but does not flatten it.
### Qualcomm Raises Prices as Margins Come Under Pressure
Alongside the Apple disclosure, Amon announced that Qualcomm will [raise prices across its entire chip portfolio beginning September 1](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/29/qualcomm-apple-modem-revenue-dropping/). He framed the move not as a margin expansion but as a cost pass-through. ["Cost went up, prices are going to go up,"](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/qualcomm-qcom-earnings-report-q3-2026-.html) Amon said. Palkhiwala estimated that [QCT Android revenue is running roughly 20 percent below prior-year levels](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29), with the memory bill-of-materials inflation imposing an EPS headwind of more than $1.50.
The memory crisis is structural, not cyclical. The same AI infrastructure build-out driving demand for high-bandwidth memory in data centers is permanently reallocating DRAM production away from mobile devices, raising costs for every smartphone maker simultaneously. Qualcomm's price increases will layer in over several quarters as customer contracts roll off — terms are negotiated individually, Amon said.
Palkhiwala acknowledged that [QCT gross margins will remain below the historical 48-to-50-percent range](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29) for the near term, with an additional 1.5-to-2-percentage-point drag expected from the initial wave of custom data center silicon, which carries margins significantly below the corporate baseline.
### Automotive: The Near-Term Replacement That Actually Works
While data center revenue dominates the strategic narrative, it is automotive that is doing the actual near-term work of replacing Apple's contribution. QCT automotive revenue reached a [record $1.59 billion in fiscal Q3 2026, up 61 percent year over year](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29), extending a multi-year streak of consecutive quarters of double-digit annual growth.
On the strength of that performance, Qualcomm [raised its automotive annualized revenue run-rate target exiting fiscal 2026 to approximately $7 billion](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29) — up from a prior guidance of $6 billion. A [new multi-generation chip supply agreement with BMW for digital cockpit systems, and an expanded collaboration with Stellantis](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29) extending into the 2030s, anchored the revision.
The [fifth-generation Snapdragon Digital Chassis, ramping in September 2026](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29), is expected to bring an order-of-magnitude increase in processing power and silicon content per vehicle — driving per-vehicle revenue above prior expectations as automakers migrate from socket-by-socket design awards to multi-generation strategic engagements. CEO Amon attributed the momentum to exactly that shift: "Customers are shifting from socket-by-socket design awards to multi-generation strategic engagements."
### Data Center: Revenue Begins in December
Qualcomm's data center ambitions are real and funded — the company spent the first half of 2026 [confirming the $3.92 billion all-stock acquisition of AI software startup Modular](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/319017/20260624/qualcomm-bets-14-billion-cracking-nvidias-ai-monopoly-risc-v-open-compiler.htm), whose Mojo programming language and MAX inference engine allow developers to run AI models across chips from multiple vendors without rewriting their code. [Meta Platforms has signed a multi-generation agreement](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/319017/20260624/qualcomm-bets-14-billion-cracking-nvidias-ai-monopoly-risc-v-open-compiler.htm) to deploy Qualcomm's Dragonfly C1000 server CPUs.
But the revenue timeline is important to hold precisely. Two unnamed hyperscale custom silicon customers already have purchase orders in hand and wafer production underway — [revenue from those engagements is expected to begin in the December 2026 quarter](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29). That is near, but it is not now. Qualcomm's stated [data center revenue target is $5 billion by fiscal 2027, rising to $15 billion by fiscal 2029](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29).
The more technically specific development from the Q3 call was the [completion of the tape-out for HBC Gen 1](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29) — Qualcomm's High Bandwidth Compute chip, which addresses a core AI inference bottleneck by integrating compute directly with high-density memory on a single package, eliminating the external DRAM accesses that currently dominate inference power consumption and cost. Silicon demonstrations are expected in coming quarters, with first solutions arriving in mid-2027. The HBC Gen 1 is the product that Amon says potential new customers need to see physically before committing to custom silicon engagements — it is the near-term pipeline's gating milestone.
**Read more:** [**Qualcomm Bets $14 Billion on Cracking Nvidia's AI Monopoly With RISC-V and an Open Compiler**](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/319017/20260624/qualcomm-bets-14-billion-cracking-nvidias-ai-monopoly-risc-v-open-compiler.htm)
### CFO: Non-Handset Revenue Growth Tops 60% in Fiscal 2027
The strategic case that Qualcomm can absorb the Apple departure rests on a single mathematical claim: [combined non-handset revenue growth](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29) — spanning automotive, IoT, data center, and adjacent segments — is forecast to exceed 60 percent in fiscal 2027, fully replacing Apple product revenue lost in fiscal 2026. By fiscal 2029, Qualcomm now targets [$40 billion in total non-handset revenue](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29), up from a prior $22 billion target, with non-handset chips projected to account for roughly two-thirds of all QCT chip revenue.
The China exposure remains a structural risk. Chinese customers accounted for [46 percent of Qualcomm's total revenues](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/320772/20260716/qualcomm-exits-small-cells-nokia-bets-nvidia-own-6g-radio-networks.htm) in its most recent fiscal year, at a time of sustained US-China trade tension. Palkhiwala said China handset revenues hit their cyclical bottom in the June quarter, with double-digit sequential growth forecast for September as channel inventory normalized — but that recovery is happening inside a market Qualcomm's CEO acknowledged is down low-teens in fiscal 2026 versus 2025.
Amon's framing at the close of the earnings call was deliberately optimistic. "We are incredibly excited about the next chapter of Qualcomm," [he told analysts](https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_QCOM_2026-07-29). "Our relevance in the next phase of AI and distributed intelligence from edge to cloud remains firmly focused on execution." The iPhone 18 lineup is expected to be unveiled at Apple's traditional September event. It will be the first generation in which Apple's own modem silicon reaches the flagship Pro tier — and the one in which Qualcomm's presence in that lineup falls to its lowest point in the company's history as an Apple supplier.
## Frequently Asked Questions
### Will the US version of the iPhone 18 Pro use a Qualcomm or Apple modem?
Based on supply chain intelligence corroborated by multiple analysts, US models of the iPhone 18 Pro are expected to retain a Qualcomm Snapdragon modem to maintain mmWave 5G performance — the high-frequency band US carriers have deployed in dense urban environments. International models are expected to use Apple's C2 modem. Apple's C2 does not yet match Qualcomm's mmWave performance, and Apple's licensing agreement with Qualcomm runs through at least March 2027. Apple has not officially confirmed modem configurations for the iPhone 18 Pro.
### Why is Apple able to make its own modems now, when it couldn't for so many years?
Apple acquired Intel's smartphone modem division in 2019 and spent six years building internal baseband expertise and intellectual property before shipping its first in-house 5G modem (the C1) in the iPhone 16e in early 2025. The delay was primarily a performance problem: Apple's early prototypes reportedly could not match Qualcomm's power efficiency or mmWave throughput. The C2, built on TSMC's 4-nanometer process, closes enough of that gap to deploy in most global markets — but the US mmWave gap persists for this generation.
### How is Qualcomm planning to replace the revenue Apple's modem business represented?
Qualcomm is running a three-track replacement strategy. In the near term, automotive revenue — at a record $1.59 billion in fiscal Q3 2026 — is already absorbing much of the impact, with a multi-year BMW digital cockpit agreement and a Stellantis partnership extending into the 2030s. In the medium term, two unnamed hyperscale data center customers are expected to begin generating revenue for Qualcomm's custom silicon in the December 2026 quarter. Long term, Qualcomm's targets call for $15 billion in annual data center revenue by fiscal 2029 and $40 billion in total non-handset revenue — nearly double its prior $22 billion target.
### What does Apple's modem independence actually mean for the iPhone's technical capabilities?
In the near term, it means the iPhone 18 Pro gains NR-NTN support in international markets — the ability to connect directly to low-earth orbit satellites for broadband internet, going well beyond the emergency satellite SOS features on current iPhones. Longer term, the strategic significance is architectural: once Apple integrates its C-series modem with the A-series application processor on a single chip package, it will be able to optimize power draw and thermal management across the full computing stack in ways that a separate third-party modem cannot match. That integration has not yet happened, but the C1 and C2 are the steps that make it possible.

## What Apple is doing about component shortages
After offering soft guidance related to "supply constraints" for parts, Cook explained how Apple is grappling with rising memory costs. It's paying more, and has done so for each of the past three quarters.
"We expect to pay even higher memory costs," Cook said.
Some of that will be offset by the inventory Apple has been holding and by expected savings on non-memory components. 
But Cook doesn't see an end in sight, and said the market should expand beyond its three primary suppliers. 
"If you look beyond September, we see the market pricing for memory continuing to increase, which could drive an increasing impact on our business," Cook said.

results.summary: PRIMARY SOURCE — European Commission factsheet (11 May 2026, DG Competition + DG CNECT). This is the single most load-bearing document for whether DMA lock-in mitigation extends beyond browsers to the PHONE-switching cost that matters for the thesis. Key finding: Apple and Google are jointly rolling out (as of late 2025/2026, still in beta as of this factsheet) a cross-OS 'device transfer' solution enabling wireless transfer of contacts, calendar, messages, PHOTOS, documents, Wi-Fi networks, passwords, AND third-party app data between iPhone and Android when switching devices — explicitly framed by the Commission as intended to 'reduce data lock-in and unlock user choice' so 'users will be able to choose a new phone based on the innovative features they value, without being locked into an ecosystem due to the complexities associated with transferring their data.' This directly targets the abandonment-of-purchased-apps/photos/data switching cost that the query identifies as the load-bearing form of lock-in (distinct from mere browser switching). HOWEVER — as of this May 2026 factsheet, the device-transfer tool (AppMigrationKit) is still in BETA/documentation-only stage for developers; it is NOT yet shown to have produced any measured switching uptake or usage statistics. This is an important absence: the Commission publishes the capability but no adoption/usage data. Preceded in 2025 by an eSIM/phone-number transfer tool (already live, multi-carrier). Also covers: mandated interoperability for connected devices (Apple Watch-equivalent notifications, proximity pairing, audio switching — due by 1 June 2026/2027) opening Apple's ecosystem privileges to third-party accessories; browser data portability via a new bidirectional API (Safari data importable into Chrome/Vivaldi on iOS) addressing app-isolation constraints unique to mobile; and draft Android interoperability measures for third-party AI assistants (wake words, system-wide access points, screen automation) under public consultation until 13 May 2026, explicitly modeled on Google's own Circle-to-Search/Gemini integration privileges. The Commission characterizes this as evidence the DMA 'continues to quietly deliver' even where changes aren't publicly attributed to it. ABSENCE TO RECORD: no EU-vs-non-EU or before/after data exists in this document (or found elsewhere in this batch) on actual iOS-to-Android switching RATES — only on the removal of switching-cost infrastructure barriers. The capability is documented; the behavioral response is not yet measured.

# Factsheet – How the DMA is making smartphones better: interoperability and data portability case studies
  * Factsheet
  * 11 May 2026
  * Directorate-General for Competition, Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology
  * 13 min read


The Commission’s enforcement of the Digital Markets Act (DMA) is delivering new interoperability and data portability features for developers and providers of connected devices (such as headphones, smartwatches, and smart glasses). As a result, iPhone and Android users can expect to see improvements in how their smartphones work over the next weeks and months. 
## New DMA data portabilitysolutions
### Full device data transfer and eSIM transfer (worldwide)
Apple and Google [have been working](https://9to5mac.com/2025/12/08/apple-and-google-team-up-to-make-iphone-and-android-switching-easier/) on a cross-OS data transfer solution that allows users to **easily move all their data when switching between an iPhone and an Android phone** (‘device transfer’). This will represent a **major upgrade** for users worldwide: currently, users who want to switch device makers face significant challenges due to the limitations of the current data transfer solutions, especially in terms of completeness of the data. 
The device transfer solution is described as allowing users to easily and wirelessly transfer data from one ecosystem to another when they set up a new device. It will support **many types of data, including contacts, calendar events, messages, photos, documents, Wi-Fi networks, passwords, and even data from third-party apps**. Apple [overviewed](https://ec.europa.eu/competition/digital_markets_act/cases/202612/DMA_100123_122.pdf) this project in its DMA compliance reports and has now made the relevant documentation available to developers in beta ([AppMigrationKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appmigrationkit)).
This solution will follow [Apple’s](https://support.apple.com/en-us/123878) and [Google’s](https://support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/16115951?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DiOS) rollout of the **eSIM transfer solution in 2025** , which greatly simplified the transfer of eSIMs and phone numbers between iPhones and Android phones (and vice versa). The solution to transfer eSIMs is already supported by several European and non-European carriers, with more to come.
Taken together, the device and eSIM transfer solutions will reduce data lock-in and unlock user choice. Users will be able to choose a new phone based on the innovative features they value, without being locked into an ecosystem due to the complexities associated with transferring their data. The device transfer solution will also benefit app developers, who will be able to easily retain their users when they change ecosystems.
Links to relevant documentation:
  * [Transfer your eSIM from Android to iPhone - Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/123878)
  * [Transfer a SIM to a new phone - Android - Pixel Phone Help](https://support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/16115951?hl=en)
  * [Perform a one-time transfer of your app’s on-device data to or from a device running another platform (AppMigrationKit)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appmigrationkit)


### Browser data portability (worldwide)
Web browsers are the apps through which users access the web. They are a crucial gateway for users of mobile devices to access digital content. To make the user experience smoother and more personalised, users can choose to store in their web browser useful data, including bookmarks, browsing history, passwords, credit card data, extensions, etc.
Users may want to switch their web browser (facilitated by a DMA choice screen), but this should not come at the cost of losing this useful data. On desktop operating systems, browser data portability has always been fairly easy: in a couple of clicks, the user can import data from one desktop browser to another. On mobile OSs, due to stricter rules related to app isolation, seamless data portability among browsers has so far not been possible.
Over the course of two years of regulatory dialogue, Apple developed two subsequent solutions to allow users to import their Safari data into another browser that is installed on the iOS/iPadOS device. The most recent solution relies on a new bidirectional API that any browser app on iOS/iPadOS can integrate with to both import and export data from and to any other browser app that also integrates with the API. 
The API-based transfer, which can be initiated by the receiving browser, happens app-to-app but is OS-mediated and user-mediated, preserving app data isolation (unlike on desktop) and avoiding the need to expose the data to the cloud. This makes this solution the first on-device data portability framework that is simultaneously user-friendly, secure, and private. 
These portability solutions have already been adopted by some third-party browsers, such as [Chrome](https://www.macobserver.com/news/chrome-on-iphone-adds-guided-safari-import/) and [Vivaldi](https://vivaldi.com/blog/vivaldi-on-mobile-7-9/), which can now offer the user to import data from Safari.
Link to relevant documentation:
  * [Export Safari data to another browser on iPhone – Apple Support (UK)](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/iphone/iph1852764a6/26/ios/26)
  * [Transferring browsing data to another browser | Apple Developer Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/browserkit/transferring-browsing-data-to-another-browser)
  * See also commentary: [Web browsers - a data portability patchwork | Data Transfer Initiative](https://dtinit.org/blog/2026/04/14/web-browsers-data-portability-patchwork)


## New DMA interoperability solutions on iOS and Android
As part of their DMA compliance, Apple, Google, (and Microsoft) have created **portals for developers to request interoperability** to features of their designated operating systems. Developers can now: 
  * **Submit** interoperability requests in [Apple’s](https://developer.apple.com/support/ios-interoperability/), [Google’s](http://developer.android.com/dma-interop-request), (and [Microsoft’s](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2271128&clcid=0x409)) portals; and
  * **Consult** interoperability requests made by other developers (if the developer agreed to make the request public) on [Apple’s](https://developer.apple.com/file/?file=interoperability-request-tracker) and [Google’s](https://issuetracker.google.com/issues?q=componentid:1520685%2B) portals.


Furthermore, the Commission **has issued**[**guidance to Apple**](https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/developer-portal/interoperability_en)**for interoperability** with iOS for connected devices and its interoperability request process. The Commission **is in the process of issuing**[**guidance to Google**](https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/commission-opens-proceedings-assist-google-complying-interoperability-and-online-search-data-sharing-2026-01-27_en)**for interoperability with Android for AI services**. 
### Interoperability with Apple iPhone for connected devices
Connected devices are a varied, large and commercially important group of products, ranging from smartwatches, headphones, virtual reality headsets, smart glasses, and more. Apple’s connected devices (e.g. Apple Watch, Vision Pro, AirPods) often have privileged access to features of Apple’s operating systems (i.e. iOS). Without access to the same features, third parties cannot compete with Apple on the merits and provide innovative products. 
Following the [Commission’s decision on connected devices](https://ec.europa.eu/competition/digital_markets_act/cases/202523/DMA_100203_1655.pdf) of 19 March 2025, Apple must release interoperability solutions for some key iOS features to allow developers and connected device providers to offer European users the same experience as with Apple’s devices.
By 1 June 2026, Apple is due to roll out new interoperability solutions for several features, including **notifications** , **proximity pairing** , and parts of the measures for **audio switching** :
  * **Notifications** are essential to ensure that users can stay informed about events, updates, reminders, and alerts from apps. They are also widely used to react and reply to messages – something that currently is only available to Apple branded connected devices, such as the Apple Watch. Users of third-party connected devices will be able to receive and react to notifications from their iPhone and make full use of their accessories. The beta version of the [Accessory Notifications framework](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accessorynotifications) was already released in iOS 26.3 (EU only).
  * **Proximity pairing** allows any connected device to pair with an iPhone through a simplified procedure. In practice, a user can simply bring a connected device (e.g. headphones) next to the iPhone, which will automatically prompt the user with a simple interface to proceed with the pairing of the device. Third-party connected devices will be able to implement this simple process, which significantly improves the user experience when users purchase, connect, and set up a new non-Apple connected device with their iPhone.
  * **Automatic audio switching** allows users to automatically switch the audio source from one device to another, e.g. from a smartphone to a computer, when using supported wireless headphones. In practice, when users who are listening to music on a device (e.g. a tablet) via wireless headphones, receive a call on the iPhone, the iPhone will automatically switch the headphone’s audio source from the tablet to the iPhone. Apple will have to expand this feature for non-connected devices by 1 June 2027.


Furthermore, in line with the deadlines set out by the Commission, Apple has **already released** (partial) interoperability solutions for **automatic Wi-Fi connection, NFC, peer-to-peer Wi-Fi** , **close-range wireless file transfer solutions** and **background execution** :
  * **Automatic Wi-Fi connection.** In iOS 26.4, Apple released the [Wi-Fi Infrastructure framework](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/wifiinfrastructure) and [Accessory Transport Extension](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/AccessoryTransportExtension) framework (EU only), which allows, subject to user consent, third-party connected devices to access the iPhone’s information about local Wi-Fi networks. The automatic Wi-Fi connection therefore allows connected devices to seamlessly join the Wi-Fi networks the iPhone is connected to, as currently possible on the Apple Watch.
  * **NFC Controller in Reader/Writer mode.** In iOS 26.0, Apple released the [NFCPaymentTagReaderSession class](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corenfc/nfcpaymenttagreadersession), which enables a number of new payment-related use cases on iPhones (EU only). For example, it allows users to use their iPhone to initiate various connected devices, such as rings or bracelets, to pay in a shop like with a payment card – without the presence of the iPhone. Users can now also use their physical credit card as an additional authentication factor when registering in a banking app, reducing the risk of fraud.
  * **High bandwidth peer-to-peer Wi-Fi connection (Wi-Fi Aware).** In iOS 26.0, Apple released the [Wi-Fi Aware framework](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/WiFiAware) (worldwide). Wi-Fi Aware is a modern and secure peer-to-peer Wi-Fi standard that allows communication with nearby devices without an internet connection. For instance, third party developers can now cast a high-resolution video from an iPhone directly to a TV or to virtual reality glasses, or share files directly between devices, even when they are not connected to the same network.
  * **Features for close-range wireless file transfer solutions.** Apple has released and updated relevant iOS frameworks (e.g. [AccessorySetupKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accessorysetupkit/), [Wi-Fi Aware](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/WiFiAware), [DeviceDiscoveryUI](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/DeviceDiscoveryUI)) toallow developers to access the same iOS-controlled features as available to Apple’s AirDrop in order to develop their own third-party file sharing app. The solution allows developers to securely pair and connect external devices to exchange files similarly to AirDrop.
  * **Background execution**. In iOS 26, Apple released an [update](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3115-bluetooth-state-restoration-app-relaunch-rules) (worldwide) to make sure that Bluetooth accessories continue working as intended when the user quits the companion app of their connected device, or when the connected device returns within range after being disconnected (e.g. when the user returns home after a run). For instance, the iPhone can now fetch the latest weather information and synchronise it to a smartwatch without requiring active user interaction (e.g. by re-opening the companion app). The iPhone can now also reliably open the user’s Bluetooth-enabled car when they get nearby the vehicle. Apple will have to provide further access to background execution on non-discriminatory terms by the end of 2026.


### Interoperability with Apple iPhone for other use cases
Apple has released more interoperability solutions in response to developers’ requests submitted via Apple’s DMA portal and following regulatory dialogue with the Commission. For example:
  * **Password managers**. Third-party password managers can now suggest strong passwords and allow the user to create a new password entry inline when they log into a new website/app, without going through a separate window (worldwide).
  * **Alarm apps**. With [AlarmKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/AlarmKit), third-party alarm apps are now able play an alarm at a specified time or when the device is muted. They are also able to display a screen overlay which gives the user an option to snooze or stop the alarm (worldwide).
  * **Memory allowance.** Apple increased the amount of memory that developers can use with [UNNotificationServiceExtension](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/unnotificationserviceextension) (worldwide). This increase was implemented in response to a [DMA request](https://ma.tt/2025/10/fight-for-open/) and allows developers to, for example, better support end-to-end encryption for push notifications.
  * **Call spam protection.** Third-party apps can now better protect users against spam calls. Apple released the [Live Caller ID Lookup app extension](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/identitylookup/livecalleridlookupextensioncontext) in iOS 18, which allows developers to provide caller ID and call-blocking services from a server that the developer maintains (worldwide).


### Interoperability with Google Android for AI services
The Commission has published draft measures that Google should implement to ensure that third-party AI services have access to the same features that are available to Google’s services. These measures are currently undergoing [public consultation](https://digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu/dma100220-consultation-proposed-measures-interoperability-google-android-article-67-dma_en). Interested developers have until 13 May 2026 to submit their views on the measures.
The measures cover several key features, including:
  * **Wake words.** The proposed measures would allow users to invoke third-party AI apps using their voice via customised wake words at any time, even when their screen is locked, with minimal impact on battery.
  * **Access points with contextual data.** The draft includes proposed measures to allow third-party apps and services to be invoked via the system-wide access points, such as long press on the home button. Those services would also receive contextual data to offer enhanced capabilities, such as translating text or searching for information on screen (as currently available to Google’s Circle to Search).
  * **App interactions and screen automation.** The proposed measures would ensure that competing AI services can interact with applications and execute tasks at the user’s request, such as sending an email using the user's preferred email app, ordering food or sharing a photo with friends.


## The DMA is delivering
The changes described above are just some examples of concrete benefits that the DMA’s interoperability and data portability obligations bring to smartphone users and app developers. There is much more that gatekeepers have implemented and will have to implement over the coming weeks and months to comply with the DMA – including new APIs for third-party earbuds to implement live translation and for media apps to provide better media casting experiences. While improvements that are DMA-driven might not always be identified as such, the DMA continues to quietly deliver on its promises by increasing user choice and creating more opportunities for everyone.
## Background
The Digital Markets Act (DMA) is an EU regulation designed to make the digital sector fairer and more contestable. It defines objective criteria for designating large digital platforms as “gatekeepers” and imposes specific obligations and prohibitions these gatekeepers must follow.
The DMA entered into force on 1 November 2022, and its obligations became applicable to designated gatekeepers in March 2024. The designated gatekeepers include Apple and Google, each designated for multiple core platform services, notably their mobile operating systems: Google’s Android and Apple’s iOS and iPadOS. 
Contestability of mobile ecosystems is a key focus area of the DMA, which imposed various requirements on Apple and Google, notably regarding interoperability, data access and portability.
The DMA requires **data portability rights** for end users via Article 6(9) DMA. Data portability is critical in the context of mobile operating systems: users store a lot of important data on their phones, and they do not want to lose this data when they buy a new phone or switch to a new app.
Similarly, the **interoperability requirement** – Article 6(7) DMA – requires gatekeepers to allow third parties to access the same OS features that are available to the gatekeeper’s own services that run on top of the OS. This is to ensure that Apple and Google no longer have exclusive access to OS features and that third-party developers can also build services and compete on the merits with the gatekeepers on their platforms. Importantly, Apple and Google remain free to decide which features are added to the OS – the DMA simply requires a level playing field. Users also remain free to decide which apps to use, and which permissions to grant to these apps.

Bear Theses 
iPhone concentration and lifecycle maturity: Apple still derives a large portion of revenue and profits from iPhone hardware sales, and improvements in replacement cycles, longer device longevity, and global smartphone saturation—especially in China and other developed markets—could compress unit growth and ASP momentum. Because Apple's operating model relies on high-margin handset volume to fund services investment and share repurchases, a sustained slowdown in iPhone demand would disproportionately pressure free cash flow and EPS growth. 
Services growth could hit a monetization ceiling inside the ecosystem: While Services (App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, AppleCare, etc.) have higher margins, their expansion depends on continued active-device growth and increasingly aggressive regulatory scrutiny (app-store fees, antitrust cases, and potential mandated third‑party app distribution). If regulators force changes to App Store economics or third-party payment routing, or if user engagement plateaus, Services revenue growth and margin contribution could fall short of expectations. 
Supply-chain, manufacturing concentration and geopolitical exposure: Apple's tight reliance on a small set of contract manufacturers and China-based assembly creates single-point risks—from COVID-like shutdowns to US‑China trade tensions and component shortages (e.g., advanced displays, modem chips). Additionally, Apple’s move toward in-house silicon and modem development raises execution and capital-intensity risks; missteps or delays could increase costs and lengthen product refresh cycles, harming margins and market share. 
Bull Theses 
Ecosystem lock-in and subscription annuity: Apple’s integrated hardware-software-services model creates high customer retention and expanding per‑user monetization. The breadth of paid subscriptions, tied to Apple ID and device family features (iCloud, AppleCare+, Apple One, Fitness+, Wallet/Apple Pay), supports recurring, high-margin revenue that is more resilient to device-cycle volatility and can steadily expand gross margins and free-cash-flow conversion over time. 
Capital returns and fortress balance sheet provide downside protection and optionality: Apple’s massive cash flows and low net leverage enable generous share repurchases, dividend increases, opportunistic M&A, and significant investment in vertical integration (custom silicon, proprietary services). This cash-generation engine both supports EPS accretion even in revenue slowdowns and funds strategic moves (chips, services, AR/health) that can drive long-term upside. 
Silicon leadership and product diversification can drive a multi-year re-rating: Apple’s vertically integrated M1/M2 architectures and ongoing investments in custom wireless/modem chips, across-device continuity features, and nascent AR/VR and health initiatives create durable differentiation. If Apple successfully extends its chip advantage and user-experience superiority into new form factors (mixed reality, wearables/health) and payments/identity, it can unlock new high-margin addressable markets and offset handset-cycle headwinds.

# iOS 27 and the iPhone Upgrade Calculus: Why Apple's AI Overhaul Could Unlock a New Supercycle
QuantumO0O May 30, 2026 0
_iOS 27, set to preview at WWDC on June 8, 2026, transforms Siri from a voice shortcut into an agentic AI platform — and in doing so, draws a hard line between iPhones that can run tomorrow's software and the hundreds of millions that cannot._
Apple's next major software release is not a design refresh. iOS 27, expected at WWDC 2026 on **June 8** and scheduled for public release in **September 2026** , is being positioned as the company's most consequential software update since iOS 7 reshaped the visual language of the iPhone in 2013.
The central change is structural: Siri is being rebuilt from the ground up into a conversational, multi-step AI agent — powered in part by Google's Gemini models — with dedicated app status, persistent chat history, and deep integration with third-party applications via an expanded App Intents framework. Analysts at Wedbush and JPMorgan view this as the ignition switch for a multi-year hardware upgrade supercycle. The math behind that thesis is straightforward: roughly **66% of all active iPhones** were running iOS 26 as of February 2026, but the most advanced Apple Intelligence features are gated behind hardware that only a fraction of that base currently owns.
Apple's overhaul of Siri in iOS 27 is expected to be the most significant change to the assistant since its 2011 launch — and the primary driver of hardware upgrade pressure in 2026–2027.
Key Fact-Check Takeaways
  * iOS 27 announced at WWDC 2026 (June 8); public release expected September 2026 alongside iPhone 18
  * Siri rebuilt as an agentic AI chatbot with dedicated app, long-term memory, and screen awareness; Gemini integration confirmed in reports
  * Apple Intelligence's advanced features limited to iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 16 series, and iPhone 17 series — requires 8GB+ RAM
  * 66% of active iPhones ran iOS 26 as of February 2026; average device replacement cycle: 3.5 years
  * Apple captured 21% of global smartphone shipments in Q1 2026 — #1 globally — with 9% YoY growth
  * Foldable iPhone (iPhone Fold/Ultra) rumored at $2,000–$2,400; analysts project $40–60B revenue in first 18 months
  * Wedbush's Dan Ives holds a $400 Apple price target; iPhone 18 pricing may rise $100–$150 per unit


## From Voice Shortcut to AI Agent: What Siri Becomes in iOS 27
The Siri announced for iOS 27 shares little with the assistant that launched in 2011. Rather than responding to isolated commands, the rebuilt Siri operates as a persistent, context-aware AI platform. It gains a standalone app — allowing users to scroll through chat history the way they would in ChatGPT — and integrates directly with the Dynamic Island, where swiping down surfaces a "Search or Ask" interface for quick queries without leaving any other app.
Screen Awareness and Cross-App Actions
The most operationally significant new capability is screen awareness: Siri in iOS 27 will be able to analyze what is currently displayed on the device and provide context-appropriate responses without the user needing to describe the situation. If a user is reading a flight confirmation email, Siri can proactively offer to add the itinerary to Calendar, find hotel options nearby, or initiate a Maps navigation — all in a single conversational thread. Across third-party apps, this is enabled through a significantly expanded App Intents framework, which Apple has been building out since iOS 16 in 2022, but which iOS 27 is expected to extend to a far broader set of app categories including banking, travel, and productivity.
Gemini Integration and the AI Model Marketplace
Reports confirm that Apple has partnered with Google to deploy Gemini models for certain Siri tasks, complementing the existing OpenAI ChatGPT integration introduced in iOS 18. iOS 27 is also expected to allow users to designate their preferred AI model — choosing between ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude (Anthropic), or Apple's native on-device models — for different task categories within a unified Settings menu. This positions Apple less as a sole AI provider and more as an AI infrastructure orchestrator for its 2.5-billion-device ecosystem.
> "Apple's installed base of 2.5 billion active devices is the most underappreciated AI asset on the planet. iOS 27 is the first software release that begins to monetize that moat in a structural way — through AI features that only the latest hardware can deliver." — Dan Ives, Senior Equity Analyst, Wedbush Securities, May 2026
Beyond Siri, iOS 27 expands Apple Intelligence into the Photos app ("Reframe" and "Extend" tools for AI-assisted photo editing), the Camera app (a dedicated Siri mode with the ability to scan nutrition labels and business cards for actionable data), and the Wallet app (user-created and customized digital passes). The breadth of these additions is notable: this is not a single-feature release but a platform transition framed around AI permeating the core OS surface area.
## The Hardware Gate: Which iPhones Actually Get the AI Features
Apple's AI ambitions in iOS 27 run directly into a physical constraint — on-device neural inference at the scale required for real-time screen awareness, multi-step task execution, and long-context Siri memory demands significant silicon resources. Apple currently specifies a minimum of **8GB of RAM** and the A17 Pro chip or newer for the full Apple Intelligence feature set.
**Apple Intelligence Compatibility Floor (iOS 27):** iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16 (all models), iPhone 17 (all models). Users on iPhone 12 through iPhone 15 non-Pro — even if their devices can install iOS 27 — will be locked out of the advanced AI features. 
Who Gets Left Behind
This hardware boundary has real implications for the scale of the addressable upgrade market. The iPhone 12, launched in October 2020, is among the devices expected to support the base version of iOS 27, but without any Apple Intelligence capabilities. iPhone 11 models and the second-generation iPhone SE are likely to be dropped from iOS 27 support entirely. Given that the average smartphone replacement cycle in 2025 was approximately **3.5 years** , a significant cohort of users who bought iPhone 12 or 13 models in 2020–2021 are now sitting precisely at the hardware threshold where upgrading makes practical sense.
66% of all active iPhones on iOS 26 as of Feb 2026
3.5 yrs average smartphone replacement cycle (2025)
The non-Pro iPhone 15 represents a particularly large stranded segment: launched in September 2023 with 6GB of RAM, it runs iOS 26 but is excluded from Apple Intelligence. Users in this cohort are within a normal upgrade window and face a concrete feature delta if they stay on their current device. Apple's iOS 17 support data suggests that devices in the 2–3 year ownership range represent the largest single upgrade cohort in any given iPhone cycle.
iOS Adoption Rate vs. Hardware Compatibility Ceiling (iOS 26, Feb 2026)
## The Installed Base Math: 2.5 Billion Devices, One Upgrade Funnel
Apple's total active device installed base surpassed **2.5 billion units** in early 2026, according to company disclosures and analyst estimates. While this figure covers all Apple hardware — iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV — the iPhone remains the center of gravity. Apple holds roughly **21% of global smartphone shipments** (Q1 2026, IDC data), making it the world's number-one smartphone brand by shipments in the first quarter for the first time, supported by **9% year-over-year shipment growth** driven by sustained iPhone 17 demand.
The retention metrics within that base are striking. Approximately **83.8% of iPhone users** report staying within the Apple ecosystem for more than five years, a loyalty rate that gives Apple an unusually captive upgrade market. Even modest conversion rates from a base of this size translate into enormous unit volumes. If iOS 27's AI feature exclusions drive even 15% of the hardware-ineligible base to upgrade within 12 months of the September 2026 release, that would represent tens of millions of incremental iPhone units.
**The "Stranded User" Calculation:** iOS 26 adoption data shows 74% of iPhones from the last four years are running the latest OS — but Apple Intelligence is only accessible on hardware shipped from September 2023 (iPhone 15 Pro) onward. Users on iPhone 12 through iPhone 15 non-Pro who want the full iOS 27 AI experience must purchase new hardware. Analysts estimate this addressable upgrade cohort at approximately 300 million devices globally.

| iPhone 12 / 12 Pro  | 2020  | 4 GB  | Yes (base only)  | No  |

| iPhone 15 (standard)  | 2023  | 6 GB  | Yes (base only)  | No  |

| iPhone 18 (all models, expected)  | 2026  | 12 GB (expected)  | Yes  | Yes (full + enhanced)  |  
## The iPhone Fold: iOS 27's Most Aggressive Hardware Statement
Apple's first foldable device — referred to in supply chain reports as the "iPhone Fold" or "iPhone Ultra" — is expected to launch in **fall 2026** , concurrently with the iPhone 18 Pro lineup. The device is designed around a book-style form factor with an internal display of approximately **7.8 inches** and an external cover display of **5.3 to 5.5 inches**. iOS 27 is being engineered in parallel, with dedicated UI adaptations including side-by-side multitasking and adaptive layout switching specifically for the foldable's dual-display architecture.
The financial projections attached to this product are substantial. Counterpoint Research and IDC analysts have estimated that Apple's foldable entry could generate between **$40 billion and $60 billion in revenue** within its first 18 months of availability — a figure that would place it among the fastest revenue ramps for any Apple hardware category. The device is expected to carry a starting price of **$2,000 to $2,400** , positioning it above the iPhone 17 Pro Max and targeting users who are already in the premium tier of the installed base.
Why iOS 27 Is Central to the Foldable Strategy
Apple's choice to co-develop iOS 27 features for the foldable form factor is strategic. By making the iPhone Fold the only device where certain multitasking and AI layout features work at their maximum capability, Apple ensures that the hardware commands its premium price through software differentiation — not just physical design. Siri's screen awareness, for instance, becomes substantially more powerful on a 7.8-inch internal display where multiple app windows are simultaneously visible.
  * Side-by-side app multitasking optimized for 7.8-inch internal display
  * Adaptive layout API for developers to build foldable-aware app interfaces
  * Siri screen awareness covering both panels simultaneously in split-view mode
  * Dynamic Island redesigned for the external 5.3-inch cover display interactions
  * Crease-reduction algorithms in Photos and video playback spanning the fold seam


## Wall Street's Supercycle Thesis: What the Numbers Actually Show
The term "supercycle" has been deployed — and misdeployed — by Apple analysts at regular intervals since the 5G transition in 2020. For iOS 27 and the iPhone 18, the thesis is more grounded in software-driven hardware exclusion than in any single breakthrough feature. Wedbush's Dan Ives has set a **$400 price target** for Apple (AAPL) as of May 2026, anchored in the view that the 2.5-billion device installed base represents "the most underappreciated AI monetization asset in consumer technology."
Revenue Vectors Beyond Hardware
The supercycle thesis is not solely about unit volumes. It has three compounding revenue vectors that analysts are modeling:
  1. **Hardware ASP expansion:** iPhone 18 is expected to carry a $100 to $150 price premium per unit relative to iPhone 17, driven by the 12GB RAM specification across all models and upgraded camera hardware. This alone represents a meaningful per-unit revenue uplift at Apple's shipment scale.
  2. **Services pull-through:** AI-specific subscription tiers — referred to as "Apple Intelligence+" in analyst models — are projected to add recurring revenue for features like extended Siri memory, higher-priority AI processing, and premium third-party model access. Adoption of Apple One and iCloud+ has already demonstrated the company's ability to attach services to hardware upgrades.
  3. **Foldable category creation:** A $2,000–$2,400 iPhone Fold with an estimated initial addressable market of 30–50 million premium-tier iPhone users globally represents a category Apple has not previously addressed, with gross margins estimated well above the standard iPhone line.


JPMorgan analysts have similarly flagged the iOS 27 cycle as a structural revenue event rather than a seasonal demand spike. The key differentiation from prior supercycle calls is the presence of a hard software-defined feature boundary — users on non-AI-capable hardware are not just missing a cosmetic upgrade, but a functional capability gap that grows with each subsequent iOS release.
Risk Factors the Bulls Acknowledge
  * Consumer price sensitivity at the $1,199+ (iPhone 18 Pro) and $2,000+ (Fold) tiers in a high-interest-rate environment
  * Regulatory scrutiny of Apple's AI model partnerships in the EU under the Digital Markets Act
  * Competitive pressure from Samsung Galaxy AI and Google Pixel AI features already shipping on Android
  * Execution risk on the foldable's crease-free display promise — Samsung and Motorola have struggled here


## What iOS 27's Rollout Timeline Means for Buyers Deciding Now
With WWDC scheduled for **June 8, 2026** , the next eight weeks will define the feature set completely. Historically, Apple's developer beta releases within 24 hours of the WWDC keynote, giving the market a detailed view of all capabilities before any hardware announcement. The public beta typically follows in July, with the GM (Golden Master) build in September alongside iPhone 18 pre-orders.
For users currently on iPhone 12, 13, or non-Pro iPhone 14/15 models, the decision calculus by September will be concrete: their hardware runs iOS 27 but is excluded from every AI feature. They will be able to see Siri's new interface on device but not initiate multi-step tasks, not access screen awareness, and not use the new Photos AI tools. Apple has historically been conservative about backporting capability — once a feature is announced as hardware-exclusive, it rarely migrates to older silicon in subsequent minor releases.
  1. **June 8:** WWDC keynote — full iOS 27 feature list confirmed, developer beta drops same day.
  2. **July 2026:** Public beta available — users on eligible hardware can test AI features before purchase.
  3. **Late August:** iPhone 18 pricing and availability announced; iPhone Fold pre-order date confirmed.
  4. **September 2026:** iOS 27 GM release alongside iPhone 18 launch — the feature gap becomes real for ineligible users.
  5. **Q4 2026:** iPhone Fold goes on sale; Apple Intelligence+ subscription tier expected to launch concurrently.


The WWDC announcement will also clarify whether iOS 27 drops the iPhone 11 and 2nd-generation iPhone SE entirely. If confirmed, those users — estimated at several tens of millions globally — will face a hard OS end-of-support deadline that adds urgency beyond the AI feature conversation.
iOS 27 represents a deliberate architectural shift in how Apple defines software value: not as a universal upgrade but as a capability tier that requires current hardware to fully unlock. For the first time, an iOS release does not simply run faster on newer devices — it fundamentally withholds core functionality from older ones.
That distinction is what gives Wedbush, JPMorgan, and the broader analyst community grounds to model a genuine multi-year upgrade acceleration, rather than the cyclical normalcy that characterized the post-5G hangover of 2022–2024. Whether the market delivers on that thesis depends entirely on whether the AI features in iOS 27 prove compelling enough in daily use to justify the hardware cost — and that question will have its first real answer in the hours after the June 8 keynote.

INTRODUCTION 
 
The general search engine has revolutionized how we live.  Information that once took 
hours or days to acquire can now be found in an instant on the internet with the help of a general 
search engine.  General search engines use powerful algorithms to create what seems like magic.  
Enter a search query, and the general search engine will retrieve, rank, and display the websites 
that provide the exact information the user seeks at that very moment.  And it all happens in the 
blink of an eye.  
 
General search engines make money by selling digital advertisements.  Type the words 
“running shoes” into a general search engine, and sellers of running shoes will compete with one 
another in a split-second auction to place an advertisement on the results page, which if clicked 
takes the user directly to the seller’s website.  This is a highly effective way of reaching consumers.  
It is also an incredibly lucrative business.  In 2021, advertisers spent more than $150 billion to 
reach users of general search engines. 
 
For more than 15 years, one general search engine has stood above the rest: Google.  The 
brand is synonymous with search.  Once a scrappy start-up founded by two Stanford University 
students in a rented garage, Google is now one of the world’s most valuable companies.  Its parent 
company, Alphabet Inc., today has a market capitalization (the value of its outstanding shares of 
stock) of more than $2 trillion.  Much of that value is due to Google’s extremely profitable 
advertising business.   
 
Google’s dominance has gone unchallenged for well over a decade.  In 2009, 80% of all 
search queries in the United States already went through Google.  That number has only grown.  
By 2020, it was nearly 90%, and even higher on mobile devices at almost 95%.  The second-place 
search engine, Microsoft’s Bing, sees roughly 6% of all search queries—84% fewer than Google.

2 
 
Google has not achieved market dominance by happenstance.  It has hired thousands of 
highly skilled engineers, innovated consistently, and made shrewd business decisions.  The result 
is the industry’s highest quality search engine, which has earned Google the trust of hundreds of 
millions of daily users.    
 
But Google also has a major, largely unseen advantage over its rivals: default distribution.  
Most users access a general search engine through a browser (like Apple’s Safari) or a search 
widget that comes preloaded on a mobile device.  Those search access points are preset with a 
“default” search engine.  The default is extremely valuable real estate.  Because many users simply 
stick to searching with the default, Google receives billions of queries every day through those 
access points.  Google derives extraordinary volumes of user data from such searches.  It then uses 
that information to improve search quality.  Google so values such data that, absent a user-initiated 
change, it stores 18 months-worth of a user’s search history and activity.   
 
The distribution agreements benefit Google in another important way.  More users mean 
more advertisers, and more advertisers mean more revenues.  As queries on Google have grown, 
so too has the amount it earns in advertising dollars.  In 2014, Google booked nearly $47 billion 
in advertising revenue.  By 2021, that number had increased more than three-fold to over 
$146 billion.  Bing, by comparison, generated only a fraction of that amount—less than $12 billion 
in 2022.        
For years, Google has secured default placements through distribution contracts.  It has 
entered into such agreements with browser developers, mobile device manufacturers, and wireless 
carriers.  These partners agree to install Google as the search engine that is delivered to the user 
right out of the box at key search access points.

3 
 
Google pays huge sums to secure these preloaded defaults.  Usually, the amount is 
calculated as a percentage of the advertising revenue that Google generates from queries run 
through the default search access points.  This is known as “revenue share.”  In 2021, those 
payments totaled more than $26 billion.  That is nearly four times more than all of Google’s other 
search-specific costs combined.  In exchange for revenue share, Google not only receives default 
placement at the key search access points, but its partners also agree not to preload any other 
general search engine on the device.  Thus, most devices in the United States come preloaded 
exclusively with Google.  These distribution deals have forced Google’s rivals to find other ways 
to reach users.   
 
Google’s dominance eventually attracted the attention of antitrust enforcers—the 
U.S. Department of Justice and nearly every state’s Attorney General.  They homed in on Google’s 
distribution agreements and in late 2020 filed two separate lawsuits alleging that the agreements 
and certain other conduct violate Section 2 of the Sherman Act.  According to their complaints, 
Google has unlawfully used the distribution agreements to thwart competition and maintain its 
monopoly in the market for general search services and in various online advertising markets.    
 
The proceedings that followed have been remarkable.  Discovery began in December 2020 
and concluded in March 2023.  Millions of pages exchanged hands, Google produced petabytes of 
data, and the parties deposed dozens of witnesses, including high-ranking executives at some of 
the world’s largest technology companies.  The court held a nine-week bench trial starting in 
September 2023.  It heard from dozens of live witnesses, including multiple experts, and admitted 
over 3,500 exhibits.  After receiving extensive post-trial submissions, the court held closing 
arguments over two days in early May 2024.  The lawyering has been first rate throughout.
